catalog_quote: [Holes 2010 p.xxiv] Word stress in Arabic depends on syllable structure. ... Short syllables: CV or CCV ... CVC ... Long syllables: CVV or CCVV ... CVVC or CVVCC ... CVCC ... [p.xxv] stress is assigned on the following basis: 1 If the word contains one long syllable only, that syllable must be stressed: gáalat, shgáalat, muDáadd, baHráyn, simá9t. 2 If the word contains two long syllables, the last one is stressed: guulúuh. 3 If the word contains no long syllable, then: (i) the ante-penultimate syllable is stressed in words of three or more ʻopenʼ syllables (i.e. that end in a vowel): báraka; (ii) the penultimate syllable is stressed in words of two syllables: smícha, Híjra, sábab and in three-syllable words if the penultimate syllable is ʻclosedʼ (i.e. ends in a consonant): warágtik, sim9áthum, sharábna. ... There is in fact a certain amount of variation in the placement of stress in ce…
